title: Bundi - The Hidden Gem of Rajasthan
content:
Bundi

Bundi is one of Rajasthan’s most charming and underrated towns.This small town, surrounded by the Aravalli Hills, is known for its magnificent forts, ancient stepwells, painted palaces, and rich cultural heritage. Unlike the more crowded cities like Jaipur or Udaipur, Bundi offers a calm and authentic experience, making it a hidden gem for travelers.

The town's main attraction is the Taragarh Fort, offering panoramic views and a glimpse into Rajasthan’s royal history. Just below it lies the Bundi Palace, famous for its vibrant murals that depict scenes from mythology and royal life. Another must-see is Rani Ji Ki Baori, a beautifully carved stepwell that showcases Bundi’s ancient water architecture.

Walking through the narrow blue-colored streets of Bundi feels like stepping into another time. The local markets are filled with traditional Rajasthani items such as miniature paintings, handmade crafts, and silver jewelry. The people here are friendly, and the slow pace of life gives you a true taste of rural Rajasthan. Don’t miss the serene Jait Sagar Lake and Nawal Sagar Lake, especially at sunset when the palaces reflect beautifully in the water.

The best time to visit Bundi is from October to March, when the weather is cool and pleasant. During this time, you can also enjoy local festivals that bring the town to life with music, dance, and color. Reaching Bundi is easy - it has a railway station connected to major cities like Kota and Jaipur. You can also travel by road from Jaipur, which takes around 4 to 5 hours. The nearest airport is in Jaipur, from where you can hire a taxi or take a bus.

Places to visit in Bundi 

1. Taragarh Fort, Bundi - The Star Fort of Rajasthan

 

The Taragarh Fort, perched on a steep hill in Bundi, Rajasthan, is one of the most impressive forts in the state, often referred to as the “Star Fort” due to its strategic location and design. Built in 1354 by Rao Deva, the founder of Bundi, this fort stands as a proud reminder of the Rajput era’s valor and grandeur.

The fort is renowned for its massive gateways, battlements, and water reservoirs that never dry up, showcasing the advanced engineering skills of the time. Its winding tunnels and secret passages add an element of mystery, while the panoramic view of Bundi city, palaces, and lakes from the fort is truly breathtaking.

Among its highlights is the Bhim Burj, a massive bastion that once mounted the renowned cannon “Garbh Gunjam” (Thunder from the Womb). The fort’s architecture, with its imposing walls and detailed carvings, reflects the artistic excellence of Rajput craftsmanship.

  • Location: Bundi, Rajasthan
  • Best Time to Visit: October - March
  • Entry Fee: ₹25 (Indians), ₹75 (Foreigners)

 

2. Raniji Ki Baori - The Queen’s Stepwell of Bundi

 

Raniji Ki Baori, also known as the Queen’s Stepwell, is one of the most impressive stepwells in Bundi, Rajasthan. Built in 1699 by Rani Nathavati Ji, the young queen of Rao Raja Anirudh Singh, this baori is not only a water reservoir but also a symbol of the architectural brilliance and cultural heritage of Bundi.

The stepwell is about 46 meters deep and is adorned with beautifully carved pillars, arched gateways, and detailed stonework. Its grand multi-storeyed design, complete with high-arched entryways and ornamented niches, reflects the grandeur of Rajput architecture. The stepwell was not just a source of water but also served as a social gathering place for locals, especially women.

Raniji Ki Baori holds spiritual significance too, as many sculptures of gods and goddesses can be seen on its walls. Today, it stands as one of Bundi’s most visited historical sites, attracting tourists, history lovers, and photographers for its architectural charm and serene ambiance.

  • Location: Near Naval Sagar, Bundi, Rajasthan
  • Timings: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM (daily)
  • Entry Fee: Indian Visitors: ₹25, Foreign Visitors: ₹100 and Camera charges extra (approx. ₹50-₹75)

 

3. Garh Palace - The Majestic Royal Residence of Bundi

 

Garh Palace, also known as Bundi Palace, is a magnificent structure situated just below the famous Taragarh Fort in Bundi. Built in the 17th century by Rao Raja Ratan Singh, the palace is an outstanding example of Rajput architecture combined with Mughal influences.

The palace is admired for its intricate murals, ornate balconies, stunning arches, and elegant courtyards. The most famous part of the palace is the Chitrashala (Hall of Paintings), which houses beautiful miniature paintings depicting stories from the Ras Lila and scenes from everyday royal life. These Bundi-style murals are considered among the best in Rajasthan.

From the palace terraces, visitors can enjoy panoramic views of Bundi town, lakes, and surrounding hills, making it a must-visit destination for history and art lovers.

  • Timings: 8:00 AM -5:00 PM (Everyday)
  • Entry Fee: Indian Visitors: ₹35 per person, Foreign Visitors: ₹350 per person & Camera Fee: ₹25 (approx.)

 

4. Sukh Mahal - The Serene Summer Palace of Bundi

 

Sukh Mahal, also called Sukh Niwas Mahal, is a beautiful palace located on the banks of the Jait Sagar Lake in Bundi. Built during the reign of Umed Singh in the 18th century, this elegant structure served as a summer retreat for the kings of Bundi.

The palace is famous for its ornate pillars, white marble chhatris, carved brackets, and delicate murals. Surrounded by lush gardens and overlooking the calm waters of the lake, it truly lives up to its name - Sukh, meaning peace and comfort.

A highlight of Sukh Mahal is the secret tunnel that is believed to connect the palace with Taragarh Fort. The serene location and architecture make it a perfect spot for history lovers as well as nature seekers.

It is also said that Rudyard Kipling, the famous English writer, stayed here during his visit to Bundi, and the beauty of the palace inspired parts of his famous novel Kim.

  • Timings: Everyday: 9:45 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indian Visitors: ₹25 per person, Foreign Visitors: ₹100 per person and Camera Fee: ₹25

 

5. Dhabhai Kund - The Stepwell of Geometric Perfection

 

Dhabhai Kund is one of the most remarkable stepwells in Bundi, located near Raniji ki Baori. Built in the 17th century, this stepwell is admired for its geometrical excellence and intricate carvings. Unlike other stepwells that are mainly functional, Dhabhai Kund is celebrated as an architectural marvel, designed with perfect symmetry and precision.

The deep stepwell is lined with stone steps in a unique pattern, creating a fascinating play of lines and shadows. The walls are decorated with delicate sculptures and carvings that depict mythological stories and motifs, reflecting the artistic brilliance of Bundi’s craftsmen.

Dhabhai Kund was not just a water reservoir but also served as a community gathering place and a symbol of prosperity for the region. Even today, it stands as a testimony to Bundi’s glorious stepwell architecture.

  • Timings: Everyday: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Indian Visitors: ₹15 per person, Foreign Visitors: ₹75 per person and Camera Fee: ₹25 (approx.)

 

6. Sadar Bazar - The Colorful Market of Bundi

 

Sadar Bazar is the main and most vibrant marketplace in Bundi, offering a lively glimpse into the town’s traditional lifestyle. Spread across narrow lanes filled with colorful shops, the bazar is a paradise for shopping lovers and culture seekers.

Here, visitors can explore a variety of items such as handmade textiles, miniature paintings, silver jewelry, wooden toys, traditional Rajasthani footwear (juttis), and handicrafts. The market is also famous for Bundi-style murals and souvenirs, making it the perfect place to collect memorable keepsakes.

Apart from shopping, Sadar Bazar is also a food lover’s delight. Small eateries and stalls serve local delicacies like kachoris, ghewar, and spicy Rajasthani snacks, giving travelers a taste of Bundi’s authentic flavors.

The market is always buzzing with activity, offering a chance to witness the vibrant culture, colors, and hospitality of Bundi in its rawest form.

  • Timings: Everyday: 10:00 AM - 8:00 PM (Best time to visit is in the evening when the bazar comes alive with lights and crowds.)
  • Entry Fee: No Entry Fee (Free to explore; pay only for shopping and food items).

 

7. Chitrashala - The Painted Gallery of Bundi

 

Chitrashala, also known as the Ummed Mahal, is one of the most famous parts of the Garh Palace in Bundi. Built by Rao Ummed Singh in the 18th century, this exquisite gallery is renowned for its Bundi-style miniature paintings, which are considered among the finest in Rajasthan.

The walls and ceilings of Chitrashala are covered with colorful murals depicting scenes from Ras Lila, Radha-Krishna tales, royal processions, hunting scenes, and festivals. The paintings are dominated by shades of green and turquoise, giving them a unique charm and vibrancy.

Unlike many palaces where murals have faded over time, the artwork in Chitrashala remains well-preserved, offering visitors a glimpse into Bundi’s rich artistic heritage. The serene setting, with a courtyard garden and open gallery, adds to its peaceful ambiance.

  • Timings: Everyday: 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: (Combined with Garh Palace ticket) Indian Visitors: ₹35 per person, Foreign Visitors: ₹350 per person & Camera Fee: ₹25

 

8. Jait Sagar Lake - The Tranquil Lake of Bundi

 

Jait Sagar Lake, located about 3 km from Bundi, is a picturesque and serene water body surrounded by the green hills of the Aravalli range. Built in the 12th century by Jaita Meena, the lake stretches for nearly 2 miles and is adorned with lotus flowers, creating a peaceful and refreshing atmosphere.

The lake is especially enchanting during the monsoon season, when the surrounding hills come alive with greenery, and the water body looks breathtakingly beautiful. On moonlit nights, the shimmering reflection of the water makes it a magical sight.

Nearby attractions include the Sukh Mahal, a charming summer palace of the Bundi rulers, which overlooks the lake and adds to its charm. This location also carries historical significance as it is believed that Rudyard Kipling stayed at Sukh Mahal during his visit and drew inspiration for his famous novel Kim.

  • Timings: Everyday: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: No Entry Fee (Free to visit; only palace or nearby attraction charges apply if visited together).

 

9. Nawal Sagar Lake - The Reflection Lake of Bundi

 

Nawal Sagar Lake, located in the heart of Bundi town, is one of the most iconic and scenic attractions of the city. This rectangular artificial lake is unique because it reflects the entire Bundi Palace and surrounding structures in its waters, creating a magical mirror-like view that enchants every visitor.

The lake is dotted with several small islands and temples, the most famous being the Varuna Temple, dedicated to the Vedic rain god, situated right at the center of the lake. The temple is partly submerged, giving it a mystical charm, especially when the water level is high.

Apart from its spiritual significance, Nawal Sagar Lake is also important as a source of water for the town in earlier times. Today, it stands as a peaceful spot for travelers, photographers, and nature lovers, offering stunning views during sunrise and sunset.

  • Timings: Everyday: Open 24 hours (Best visited early morning or evening for photography and peaceful ambiance)
  • Entry Fee: No Entry Fee (Free for visitors).

 

10. Shikar Burj - The Royal Hunting Lodge of Bundi

 

Shikar Burj, located about 2 km from Bundi, is a historic hunting lodge built by the rulers of Bundi as their retreat. Nestled amidst serene greenery and away from the hustle of the town, it was once the spot where Bundi kings indulged in hunting expeditions and leisure time.

The structure is simple yet charming, with an old-world appeal, surrounded by dense forests and quiet landscapes. Unlike the grand palaces of Bundi, Shikar Burj offers a more rustic glimpse into the royal lifestyle, reflecting their passion for hunting and nature.

Today, it stands as a peaceful spot for travelers seeking solitude and is a popular picnic location among locals. Its tranquil surroundings and natural beauty make it a nice stop for those exploring Bundi beyond its forts, stepwells, and palaces.

Timings: Everyday: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM

Entry Fee: No Entry Fee (Free for visitors).

 

11. Hathi Pol - Bundi, Rajasthan

 

Hathi Pol (meaning Elephant Gate) is the grand and historic entrance to the Garh Palace in Bundi, Rajasthan. True to its name, the gateway features two large, beautifully sculpted elephants that seem to stand guard at the top of the arch - a classic symbol of royal authority and protection.

Built during the reign of the Hada Rajput rulers, Hathi Pol served as a ceremonial entrance for kings and nobles. Passing through this gate takes you into the Garh Palace, a stunning complex filled with frescoes, jharokhas (balconies), and the famous Chitrashala (Painted Gallery), showcasing Bundi’s renowned miniature paintings.

Surrounded by hills and overlooking the town, the entire palace-including Hathi Pol-offers a glimpse into Rajasthan’s regal past and architectural brilliance.

  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Open all days)
  • Entry Fee (for Garh Palace, including Hathi Pol): Indian Citizens: ₹80 - ₹100 Foreign Nationals: ₹350 - ₹500 (Camera/Video charges may apply separately)
  • Location: Garh Palace Complex, Bundi, Rajasthan
  • Tip: Hiring a local guide is recommended to understand the history and art within the palace.

 

12. 84 Pillared Cenotaph - Chaurasi Khambon ki Chhatri

 

The 84 Pillared Cenotaph, locally known as Chaurasi Khambon ki Chhatri, is one of Bundi’s most iconic and architecturally unique monuments. Built in 1683 by Maharaja Anirudh Singh, this elegant memorial was dedicated to his foster brother, Deva, a respected figure in the royal court.

As the name suggests, the structure is supported by 84 intricately carved pillars, each uniquely designed. The cenotaph features a beautiful domed pavilion adorned with delicate stone carvings, including floral patterns and religious motifs. The number 84 holds symbolic significance in Hinduism, often associated with the spiritual cycle of rebirth.

Set in a serene area just outside the main city, the cenotaph offers a peaceful glimpse into Bundi’s royal history and artistic heritage.

  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Daily)
  • Entry Fee: Indian Nationals: ₹20 - ₹50 and Foreign Tourists: ₹100 - ₹200
  • Location: Near Azad Park, Bundi, Rajasthan
  • Photography: Allowed (camera charges may apply)
  • Tip: Visit during early morning or late afternoon for best lighting and fewer crowds.

 

13. Moti Mahal - The Palace of Pearls 

 

Moti Mahal, meaning Palace of Pearls, is one of the most stunning structures within the Garh Palace complex in Bundi. Built by Raja Raja Ratan Singh, this beautiful palace was used as a royal residence and for courtly gatherings.

The name "Moti Mahal" reflects the elegance of its interiors - known for glittering mirror work, intricate murals, and ornate arches that create a pearlescent glow in the natural light. The palace offers panoramic views of the town of Bundi, the surrounding Aravalli hills, and the scenic Nawal Sagar Lake below.

Inside, you can admire the frescoes and Bundi-style miniature paintings, which depict royal life, mythology, and local traditions in vivid detail. Though partially weathered by time, Moti Mahal still holds the charm and grandeur of Bundi’s royal past.

  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Daily)
  • Entry Fee: Included in Garh Palace ticket (₹80-₹100 for Indians, ₹350-₹500 for foreigners)
  • Location: Inside Garh Palace, Bundi, Rajasthan
  • Photography: Allowed (camera/video charges may apply)
  • Tip: A local guide can help explain the symbolism in the murals and architecture.

 

14. Badal Mahal -The Palace of Clouds

 

Badal Mahal, or “Palace of Clouds,” is one of the most enchanting parts of the Garh Palace complex in Bundi. Perched high on the palace walls, this structure was designed to give the feeling of being amidst the clouds - offering breathtaking views of Bundi town, the surrounding hills, and the lake below.

The palace features beautiful frescoes, wall paintings, and intricate mirror work, characteristic of the Bundi School of Art. These murals depict royal processions, hunting scenes, and mythological tales, all painted in rich natural colors that have lasted centuries.

Badal Mahal is a quieter part of the palace complex, giving visitors a chance to soak in the artistry and serenity without the crowds.

  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Open daily)
  • Entry Fee: Included in Garh Palace ticket ₹80-₹100 for Indian visitors , ₹350-₹500 for foreign tourists
  • Location: Upper section of Garh Palace, Bundi, Rajasthan
  • Photography: Allowed (extra charges may apply)
  • Tip: Don’t miss the murals - a local guide can help you understand their historical and cultural meanings.
excerpt: Bundi is a lesser-known town in Rajasthan filled with history, art, and architecture. Visit stunning forts, stepwells, and colorful streets away from tourist crowds. A perfect offbeat destination for culture lovers and peace seekers.
